title: Exactly-once, as it is
dek: A Kafka transaction is two logs agreeing after the fact: a decision in one, markers in others, a stall in between. This last part of a five-part teardown reads Apache Kafka 4.4.0 and takes one apart byte by byte: the coordinator's state machine, Transaction Version 2, a 78-byte marker, the last stable offset that stalls plain records too, the epoch fence, and KAFKA-20734, known upstream, where a marker for an offline partition is dropped and the coordinator says complete. That bug has no tagged fix as of 6 November 2026. The part ends where exactly-once ends, and with the whole collection's findings register.
byline: 6 November 2026 · Subject: kafka@1156b275 (Apache Kafka 4.4.0) · Part 5 of 5 · Read from the source; measured where this machine allows
description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 5: the transaction coordinator, TV2, control markers on disk, the last stable offset, epoch fencing, hanging transactions and KAFKA-20734, what exactly-once does not cover, and the collection's findings register.
og_description: Part 5 of a five-part Kafka teardown at kafka 1156b275 (4.4.0): commitTransaction returning means decided, not visible; one open transaction stalls plain records too; and KAFKA-20734, known upstream and untagged as of 6 November 2026, hides committed records from read_committed while the bytes stay.
